learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Fourier Transform.
Apply Fourier Transform to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: The Fourier transform decomposes a time-domain waveform into sinusoidal frequency components.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: It assumes stationarity within the analysed window and loses exact temporal localisation. Windowing and epoch length affect frequency resolution and spectral leakage.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Underpins spectral power analysis and helps clinicians understand what band metrics actually represent.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: A spectrum cannot show when a transient occurred within the epoch.

reviewPrompts.answer: It assumes stationarity within the analysed window and loses exact temporal localisation. Windowing and epoch length affect frequency resolution and spectral leakage.
Underpins spectral power analysis and helps clinicians understand what band metrics actually represent.

Frequency decomposition is a mathematical lens, not a direct list of brain modules.
